paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: wisdom is mostly about what you do with ordinary days. The wise say to be fair when you judge, to give an honest answer, and to leave the comeback unsaid. Every one of those sayings asks the same thing of you: do the right thing even when the crooked thing is easier (Proverbs 24:23, 26, 29).

Then the writer walks past a field and gets a whole sermon without a single word spoken. Thorns everywhere, and a stone wall that is "broken down" (Proverbs 24:31). Nobody planned that mess. It came from "a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest" (Proverbs 24:33). I think that's the sneaky part, because no single nap looks like the problem.

So here's what I want you to take with you, baker. Small choices add up, whether it's an honest word today or one more snooze tomorrow. Poverty comes "like a robber" (Proverbs 24:34), and I'd rather you be up and working when it knocks. Tend your field, tell the truth, and keep those ovens ready!
